text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to pick between two Q2 initiatives: (A) 'Dedicated autoscale + burst' (heavy infra work) vs (B) 'Private quickstart (VPC onboarding lite)' (customer acquisition). Headcount is tight. I started a quick RICE draft below, can folks sanity-check?

kevin: Thx. Drop the draft pls. I can eyeball the effort estimates.

maya: Paste:
```
Initiative | Reach | Impact (1-10) | Confidence | Effort (person-weeks) | RICE score
A. Autoscale+burst | 2,400 requests/day (prod customers) | 7 | 0.7 | 24 pw | (Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort
B. VPC quickstart | 6 new enterprise customers/mo | 6 | 0.6 | 12 pw | same formula
```

lia: Quick note — Reach units are different; convert to ARR-ish to compare. For B we should use "net new ARR/month" (avg $5k/mo/customer) => Reach ~30k. For A the customer value is harder: reduces per-token cost for enterprise apps, estimate $15k/yr saved across customers => Reach ~180k annually? kinda fuzzy.

kevin: Agree on normalization. For effort, 24 pw for autoscale assumes 2 eng + 1 infra for 6 weeks. We might cut to 18 pw if we scope to MVP (no UI).

maya: Updated assumptions: A effort -> 18 pw, Impact A->8, Confidence 0.6 (kernel/ops unknown). B effort 12 pw, Impact 6.5, Confidence 0.8. Can someone compute RICE quickly?

sam: Quick calc:
- A: Reach 180 (k$) * Impact 8 * 0.6 / 18 = (180*8*0.6)/18 = (864)/18 = 48
- B: Reach 30 (k$) * Impact 6.5 * 0.8 / 12 = (30*6.5*0.8)/12 = (156)/12 = 13
Numbers are rough but A >> B on normalized RICE.

ashley: UX/Docs effort for B is nontrivial — onboarding flow & sample connectors ~3 pw more. If B is actually 15 pw it drops further.

kevin: Important counterpoint: A requires eng-infra schedule coordination and will block other platform work for 6 weeks. We have two high-priority customer bugs that need 1 full-time engineer for 4 weeks. If we take A now, those bugs slip. That has CRO/CS impact.

maya: Right — RICE pushed A, but sequencing risk and cross-team deps might favor B because it's less blocking. Product tradeoff: higher net economic value vs lower cross-team friction.

lia: Also risk: A's Confidence 0.6 due to unknown regression risk in runtime path. If a regression causes customer outages, cost is huge. We should add a penalty to A for production risk.

eng-infra-bot: FYI: upcoming infra window (week of 1770000000) reserved for kernel patch; autoscale changes would need signoff, possible merge conflicts.

maya: Proposal: split into two lanes: do a 3-week spike for A (2 engineers, prove non-regression on canary) + keep B as a short 6-week deliverable by DRI PM + 1 FE + 1 SDK. Spike cost ~6 pw; if results are green, schedule full A next quarter. That balances RICE and sequencing.

kevin: I can do the spike but can't commit full ownership for full A this quarter. +1 to spike.

sam: I'll reserve staging capacity for the spike canary and prebook the infra window with eng-infra. Put me as owner for canary runbooks.

lia: I'll run a quick regression risk model and produce a short checklist for the spike (KV cache tests, long-tail latency tests).

ashley: I'll scope the B quickstart UX and see if we can reduce docs work by shipping a templated CloudFormation + 1-click script. Might hit 9 pw -> still doable.

maya: OK decision: APPROVE 3-week autoscale spike (maya, kevin, sam, lia) + proceed with trimmed B (quickstart) in parallel but deprioritize aggressive marketing until we confirm. Owners: maya (PM), kevin (eng spike lead), ashley (quickstart UX), sam (infra canary).

kevin: I'll post a short RFC for the spike with success criteria: no regression in 2-week canary, <10% p95 latency increase, and automated rollback.

maya: Thanks — can everyone add blockers to the RFC by EOD tomorrow? I'll update roadmap board and re-run RICE after spike. :calendar: :+1: 

lia: Adding checklist now.

sam: Booked infra window, pinged infra leads.

eng-infra-bot: infra window confirmed: 1770000000-1770003600. Merge gating applied.

maya: Great — closing thread. We will reconvene after spike for final sequencing decision.
